Heavy Rainfall Warning No. 15 #NCR_PRSD
Weather System: Enhanced Southwest Monsoon (Habagat) and Severe Tropical Storm CRISING
Issued at: 11:00 AM, 19 July 2025(Saturday)

ORANGE WARNING LEVEL: Zambales, Bataan, Tarlac, Pampanga, Bulacan, Metro Manila, Cavite and Rizal.
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: FLOODING is still THREATENING.

YELLOW WARNING LEVEL: Nueva Ecija, Batangas and Laguna.
ASSOCIATED HAZARD: FLOODING in flood-prone areas.
Meanwhile, light to moderate with occasional heavy rains affecting Quezon which may persist within 3 hours.
The public and the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Offices concerned are advised to MONITOR the weather condition and watch for the next warning to be issued at 2:00 PM today.

For more information and queries, please call telephone numbers 8927-1335 and 8927-2877 or log on to https://t.co/59mTpZJq1n.

data.text:
The Legendaddies questions the logic of harsh penalties for cannabis use in the Philippines—especially when alcohol and cigarettes remain legal despite their social costs. Reflecting on extortion, fearmongering, and outdated laws, he argues that responsible, adult access to cannabis shouldn't be criminalized.

With all the daily frustrations Filipinos endure—traffic, systemic corruption, inequality—shouldn't people have a safer outlet than alcohol? This isn't about pushing a party drug, he suggests. It's about sanity, sovereignty, and a fairer future.

BAHA SA TAFT

The stretch of Taft Avenue in Manila turned into a river early Saturday morning, with gutter-deep flooding caused by heavy rains from the southwest monsoon enhanced by Severe Tropical Storm #CrisingPH.

Several motorists and commuters struggled with the rising water, while some passengers had difficulty boarding buses.

📸 The STAR/Edd Gumban
